{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 134,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Date override availability skips busy-time check",
      "body": "In checkIfIsAvailable, when dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is not rejected by the date-override predicate, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. This means any busy time from bookings, calendars, or other sources is ignored for slots covered by a date override. A host who is already busy can still be shown as available, which can lead to invalid slot offers and double-booking risks."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours check rejects slots if any interval does not contain them",
      "body": "workingHours.find is used as if it detects whether a slot is outside working hours, but the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside the current working-hour interval. If a user has multiple working-hour intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval will be outside another interval and the whole check returns false, hiding valid availability. Conversely, if there is no working-hour entry for that weekday, the check falls through and treats the slot as available. The logic should require that at least one working-hour interval fully contains the slot."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 142,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours check ignores event duration",
      "body": "The end variable is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. This checks only the start of the slot against working hours and allows slots whose end time falls after the working-hour boundary. As a result, events that begin inside availability but extend past it can be marked available."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date-override containment allows partially overlapping slots",
      "body": "The date-override check only rejects slots that end before or exactly at the override start, or start after the override end. It does not reject slots that start before the override start or end after the override end. It also treats a slot starting exactly at the override end as valid because isAfter is used instead of an isSame-or-after boundary check. Therefore, slots that only partially overlap a date override can pass availability."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Multiple date overrides for the same day are not handled correctly",
      "body": "The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns true for the first override that the slot is outside. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the second override can be rejected because it is outside the first override, and find stops at that first rejection. Availability with multiple per-day overrides will be incorrect."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 114,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Dayjs objects compared with ===",
      "body": "The zero-length override check compares two dayjs instances with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for separately created dayjs objects. The intended start-equals-end handling will never trigger; use isSame() instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 212,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "getSlots now relies on optional timeZone being populated",
      "body": "TimeRange.timeZone was added as an optional field, but getSlots now calls dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone) unconditionally. Only the trpc slots router was updated to populate timeZone on date overrides. Other callers of getSlots that pass DateOverride objects without timeZone may get invalid timezone handling, incorrect slots, or runtime failures. The type should make this requirement explicit or the code should safely fall back."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 219,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Timezone-converted overrides can lose cross-midnight information",
      "body": "Override start and end times are converted to minutes using hour() * 60 + minute() after applying a timezone offset. If the timezone conversion moves an override across local midnight, the date portion is discarded. endTime can become numerically smaller than startTime, causing buildSlots to skip the range, or the override can be attached to the wrong invitee day. This makes late-night overrides unreliable for invitees in different timezones."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts",
      "line": 788,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No automated test for the fixed-host round-robin date override fix",
      "body": "The added test only checks a personal event date override in a different invitee timezone. The PR's primary stated fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must constrain round-robin availability, but there is no test with a round-robin event, a fixed host, and a date override. There is also no test that busy times still block slots inside date overrides. This leaves the main behavior and the critical busy-time interaction untested."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 484,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "fixedHosts is recomputed for every slot",
      "body": "Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for every slot. The set of fixed hosts does not change during the request. Hoisting this computation outside the slot filter avoids repeated O(number_of_slots * number_of_users) filtering."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 531,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "typeof result compared to undefined instead of a string",
      "body": "The condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined is always true because typeof returns a string, and the later condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats === undefined is always false. If currentSeats is undefined while occupied seats exist, the code can call map or push on undefined and crash. The checks should compare against the string 'undefined' or use availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined directly."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Date override availability skips busy-time check
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is not rejected by the date-override predicate, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. This means any busy time from bookings, calendars, or other sources is ignored for slots covered by a date override. A host who is already busy can still be shown as available, which can lead to invalid slot offers and double-booking risks.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots if any interval does not contain them
findings.body: workingHours.find is used as if it detects whether a slot is outside working hours, but the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside the current working-hour interval. If a user has multiple working-hour intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval will be outside another interval and the whole check returns false, hiding valid availability. Conversely, if there is no working-hour entry for that weekday, the check falls through and treats the slot as available. The logic should require that at least one working-hour interval fully contains the slot.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores event duration
findings.body: The end variable is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. This checks only the start of the slot against working hours and allows slots whose end time falls after the working-hour boundary. As a result, events that begin inside availability but extend past it can be marked available.

findings.title: Date-override containment allows partially overlapping slots
findings.body: The date-override check only rejects slots that end before or exactly at the override start, or start after the override end. It does not reject slots that start before the override start or end after the override end. It also treats a slot starting exactly at the override end as valid because isAfter is used instead of an isSame-or-after boundary check. Therefore, slots that only partially overlap a date override can pass availability.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are not handled correctly
findings.body: The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns true for the first override that the slot is outside. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the second override can be rejected because it is outside the first override, and find stops at that first rejection. Availability with multiple per-day overrides will be incorrect.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with ===
findings.body: The zero-length override check compares two dayjs instances with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for separately created dayjs objects. The intended start-equals-end handling will never trigger; use isSame() instead.

findings.title: getSlots now relies on optional timeZone being populated
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone was added as an optional field, but getSlots now calls dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone) unconditionally. Only the trpc slots router was updated to populate timeZone on date overrides. Other callers of getSlots that pass DateOverride objects without timeZone may get invalid timezone handling, incorrect slots, or runtime failures. The type should make this requirement explicit or the code should safely fall back.

findings.title: Timezone-converted overrides can lose cross-midnight information
findings.body: Override start and end times are converted to minutes using hour() * 60 + minute() after applying a timezone offset. If the timezone conversion moves an override across local midnight, the date portion is discarded. endTime can become numerically smaller than startTime, causing buildSlots to skip the range, or the override can be attached to the wrong invitee day. This makes late-night overrides unreliable for invitees in different timezones.

findings.title: No automated test for the fixed-host round-robin date override fix
findings.body: The added test only checks a personal event date override in a different invitee timezone. The PR's primary stated fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must constrain round-robin availability, but there is no test with a round-robin event, a fixed host, and a date override. There is also no test that busy times still block slots inside date overrides. This leaves the main behavior and the critical busy-time interaction untested.

findings.title: fixedHosts is recomputed for every slot
findings.body: Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for every slot. The set of fixed hosts does not change during the request. Hoisting this computation outside the slot filter avoids repeated O(number_of_slots * number_of_users) filtering.

findings.title: typeof result compared to undefined instead of a string
findings.body: The condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined is always true because typeof returns a string, and the later condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats === undefined is always false. If currentSeats is undefined while occupied seats exist, the code can call map or push on undefined and crash. The checks should compare against the string 'undefined' or use availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined directly.
